title: How to take a screenshot automatically when saving the game ( RPG Maker MV )?

posts.author: GrentoYTP
posts.body:
Hi everyone,
I'm currently working on a project in RPG Maker MV, and I'm trying to implement a feature where the game takes a screenshot automatically when the player saves the game.
The idea is similar to what you see in games built with the GZDoom engine — when you save your game, a thumbnail or screenshot is generated and later shown next to each save file in the load/save menu. I’d love to find a workaround or plugin-based solution.
What I’d like to achieve:
When the player saves the game, a screenshot of the current screen is automatically taken.
The screenshot is saved (e.g. as a .png file) with the same name as the save file or in a dedicated folder.
(Optional) Later, I could use that image to display a small preview in a custom load menu.
If anyone knows of a plugin or script snippet that could help me capture the screen at the moment of saving, I'd really appreciate it. I'm comfortable modifying code if needed.
Thanks in advance for any help or ideas!

Actually, I’d like to make it look just like in the "SaveGameMenu" — where it currently says “no picture”, I’d like to display a screenshot from the moment the player saves the game.
The same goes for both the save menu and the load menu.
In my project (screenshot), just below the load/save/delete options, there’s a black area — that’s exactly the space I’d like to fill with an actual image from the game at the time of saving.
Also, I should mention that I’m using GraphicalDesignMode to create this custom interface. It works really well visually, but now I’m trying to take it a step further by having real-time screenshots linked to each save file.
If anyone knows how to capture and store a screenshot when saving — and then display it per save slot — that would help a lot.
Thanks in advance!

If you’re able to create a plugin that displays a screenshot of the game at the moment of saving — one for each save slot — I’d be very grateful. That’s exactly what I’m looking for. You can prepare such a demo — I’d really appreciate it.
